newsitem.title: MEXICO: GMexico-led group bids for Pacific-North railway.
newsitem.headline: GMexico-led group bids for Pacific-North railway.

text.p: A consortium led by Grupo Mexico on Thursday offered 3.15 billion pesos for a concession to operate Mexico's Pacific-North railway, above the minimum required bid.

The consortium, called Grupo Ferroviaria Mexicana (GFM), is composed of miner Grupo Mexico, with a 74 percent stake, and Mexican builders Empresas ICA and U.S. Union Pacific Corp, which each have a 13 percent stake in the bid.
The government said at a ceremony that the minimum bid was 2.71 billion pesos. Officials said final approval of the bid by the GMxico-led group, the only bidder, was subject to a technical study.
Officials did not say when final approval might be granted.
The railway is Mexico's largest with 3,875 miles (6,200 km) of rail and connects five U.S. border cites with key industrial cities and port sites.
The government said at a ceremony that the minimum price established for the concession, including 80 percent of the rail line's assets, was 2.71 billion pesos.
Officials said final approval of the bid by the GMxico-led group, the only bidder, was subject to a technical study. They did not say when final approval might be granted.

After the government announced the GMexico bid, it clarified that the consortium had actually expanded its bid and was seeking 100 percent control of the rail line. The concession was originally for 80 percent of the line's assets, but the bidders had an option for full control.
In addition, the group said it wanted to buy the Topolobampo-Ojinaga rail line as well and offered $527.39 million for the whole package.

"GFM exercised the option to acquire ahead of time the remaining 20 percent of the rail's stock at the price of the sale of the (other 80 percent)," Mexico's state-owned Ferrocarriles Nacionales de Mxico said in a statement.
"They also made clear their intention to keep its option to buy the short line Ojinaga-Topolobampo," it added.

The privatization of the Pacific-North is the second of three railway lines to be sold. On Monday, the government handed over the assets of the Northeast Railway, a smaller route parallel to the Pacific-North on the country's eastern flank.
